How to name nested components

Nested component instances inside another component must have semantic names to differentiate them.

For example, the ‘Level’ links and the ‘Separator’ in the breadcrumb are instances of subcomponents and they need to be differentiated.

This rule doesn't apply when multiple instances of a component are inside a frame named ‘List container’.


savings  Mandatory rule
standardOnBackground  Checked by plugin
When to use a ‘List container’ frame & how to name nested components inside it

When building a component that could have a list of multiple instances of a subcomponent, you should keep the instance name as is, and name the parent frame of the instances as ‘List Container’.

For example, if you are using multiple instances of a tag, they should all be under a ‘List Container’ frame.

You should only name a parent frame ‘List container’ if the instances are part of a list.

How to name component sets

Name your component sets starting with the acronym set in the plugin settings. 

For example, OneID component sets start with the acronym ODS.

When creating your own component sets, use the specific acronym for your product, as set in the plugin settings.


warning  Best practice
How to name properties

Select descriptive property names that indicate the effects on components.

For example, use names like 'Show Icon' for a boolean controlling icon visibility. If multiple icons exist, specify with 'Icon Left' or 'Icon Right'.

Variant property names are used for visual changes or changes to the elements within a component, without significantly impacting the use case or functionality.

Type property names are used for different functions.

Case 1: You can consider the basic type as a functional variant, meaning that switching the basic type affects the function of a component.
Case 2: Additionally, this property is used when the use case of a component is drastically changing.
The 'Mode' property name is used for indicating the notification states of the component.
